A reviewer observation captured during the run mentions drift in the
nonblocking router. The bash heuristic regex previously routed this to
the non-blocking sweep because the body contains the words "observation"
and "drift" — words that are reviewer vocabulary, not CI vocabulary.

The CI signal that the test failed lives only in the artifact header:
the bash heuristic never scanned Header in isolation.

This fixture is the exact case the m21 closeout drift entry described.
The Go router routes it as Blocking because the explicit [FAIL]
sentinel in the header takes precedence over the heuristic chain.
